newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished a lackluster session mostly lower, as the overall equities market remained unimpressed with the rally in U.S. T-bonds, traders and analysts said.
December Standard & Poor 500s clung to narrow intraday ranges that were carved out in the first half of pit trade.
They said heavy selling by two large U.S. firms throughout the day kept the December contract on the defensive.
One U.S. firm steadily sold 2,200 December S&Ps throughout the session, and was reportedly buying T-bonds, several traders said.
Another firm sold a total of 700 contracts throughout the day, which kept a lid on any attempts by locals to drive the market higher, traders said.

Nikkei futures remained strong, however, with December closing at the day's high of 21,475.0. Traders attributed the contract's gains to the U.S. dollar's appreciation against the yen. Dealers covered short dollar positions against the yen into the afternoon, traders said.
Traders are awaiting Thursday's weekly U.S. jobless claims data and U.S. August durable goods report, which will both be released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
Fair value for December is at 5.75 points to cash.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were down 1.00 at 691.05, New Composites were down 0.30 at 367.30, Value Lines were up 0.40 at 640.40, Nikkeis were up 285.0 at 21,475, and Midcap 400s were down 0.10 at 241.95. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
